name: color-extraction
description: Upload an image and get its dominant colors as [{hex, percentage}] sorted by coverage. Near-identical colors are grouped by snapping each channel to a small grid, so the result is a handful of meaningful swatches rather than thousands of near-duplicates. The pure-Python core (extract_from_pixels) is dependency-free and tested; extract_colors() reads a file via Pillow (optional [image] extra). Feeds color-matching (the dominant/skin tone becomes the seasonal input).
shortDescription: Extract an image's dominant colors with their coverage percentages.
keywords: dominant color extraction from an image

name: color-matching

SEASONAL (primary): from a base color's undertone + value, classify the season and return the season's recommended palette and colors to avoid — the Color-Matching app's core (skin tone -> 'your colors'). HARMONIES (secondary): complementary, analogous, triadic, split-complementary, tetradic, and monochromatic schemes off a base color. Pure Python (stdlib colorsys), no dependencies.
shortDescription: Classify a color into a season (Spring/Summer/Autumn/Winter) with its palette and colors to avoid, plus classic harmonies.

name: Foundations
description: The lowest design layer — the raw decisions the tokens are derived from: color, typography, spacing, radius, elevation, motion, accessibility, breakpoints, grids. Foundations are *expressed* as machine-readable tokens in `../tokens/` (W3C DTCG); this folder documents the **rationale and rules** behind them. Humans set foundations here; agents only ever touch the derived tokens. - `color-rules.md` — how palettes are computed (not hand-picked); harmonies, 60-30-10, WCAG. - `typography.md` — the four type roles and the hierarchy rules. - `spacing.md` — the 4-pt spacing scale, radius, and elevation. - `accessibility.md` — contrast gate, hit targets, Dynamic Type, VoiceOver. - `materials.md` — Liquid Glass translucency (the `material.*` tokens). - `motion.md` — animation durations + easing (the `motion.*` tokens). - `breakpoints.md` — size classes + width thresholds (the `breakpoint.*` tokens). - `grids.md` — margins, gutters, columns, readable width.

name: legal
description: Generates a **Privacy Policy** + **Terms & Conditions** for an app from its data-use profile. Deterministic template filling — **not legal advice**. Every document is stamped *"requires human/legal review before publishing"* and `generate()` returns `review_required=True`. Why it exists: the App Store **requires a privacy policy** (Guideline 5.1). The compliance agent only *checks* for one; this produces a truthful first draft grounded in what the app actually does — especially **on-device** processing (no server → strong, honest privacy stance). Placeholders left as `[COMPANY]`, `[JURISDICTION]`, etc. are surfaced in `warnings` so nothing ships half-filled. **A lawyer must review the output before it goes live.**

name: rag
description: A small, **dependency-free** retrieval library for grounding agents in a document corpus. - **`Corpus`** — documents chunked into pieces, each carrying its `source` (for citations). - **`load_corpus(dir)`** — index every `*.md` (uses a `source:` line as the citation URL). - **`LexicalRetriever`** — TF-IDF cosine over chunks. name: ux-attention-pattern
description: Tuned for iOS app screens (narrow, vertical, component-driven), grounded in NN/g eye-tracking research + Apple HIG. Uses the attention modules (vis_models.saliency — real SUM when weights are on the box, else the classical pixel model, else the deterministic mock) to predict a screen's attention, then classifies the reading flow from the grid's row/column profiles: vertical (layer-cake column of sections — good), gutenberg (top anchor + bottom terminal CTA in the thumb zone — good), focused (single hero/action — good), f-skim (top-left text-wall skim — warn), scattered (no hierarchy — bad). If a cta point is given, a gutenberg/vertical screen is only fully good when attention reaches the CTA. The rule core (classify_pattern) is pure stdlib; the image layer depends on vis_models.saliency.
shortDescription: Run a screen through the attention modules and decide which iOS reading flow it follows, and whether that's healthy.
keywords: classify an iOS screen's reading pattern (vertical/gutenberg/f-skim/focused/scattered) and judge it

name: ux-position-mask
description: Audits which elements of a screen are in good vs dangerous positions. Core rules (`audit`, pure stdlib): given elements with a role (primary/secondary/content) and a normalized box, return a per-element verdict (good/ok/dangerous) with reasons plus a score/grade — thumb-reach ergonomics (primary actions belong lower-center), rule-of-thirds active zones (key content where the eye lands first), and safe areas (status bar/notch, home indicator, edges). For an arbitrary screen *design*, `audit_image(path)` first runs a classical, offline detector (background subtraction + connected components + role heuristics; Pillow/numpy/scipy) to find the elements, then scores them. Migration path: when auditing *generated* screens, replace detection by reading element boxes from the known layout — the rules stay the same.
